Paragraph: Such a man of understanding acts with mind and intelligence perfectly controlled, gives up all sense of proprietorship over his possessions and acts only for the bare necessities of life. Thus working, he is not affected by sinful reactions.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The fear of material attachment, possessiveness, and accruing negative reactions while maintaining bodily existence.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'Such a man of understanding acts with mind and intelligence perfectly controlled, gives up all sense of proprietorship over his possessions and acts only for the bare necessities of life. Thus working, he is not affected by sinful reactions.'
Outcome/Resolution: By surrendering psychological ownership and acting purely for basic maintenance, one achieves complete freedom from karmic reactions.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mindful Self-Control: Regulating thoughts and mental energy to prevent emotional overreaction
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Non-Possessiveness: Releasing psychological ownership over external objects and outcomes
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Minimalism for Mental Peace: Focusing effort only on basic necessities to reduce cognitive burden

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sariram kevalam karma (Acting only for the bare maintenance of the body)
Naapnoti kilbisam (Does not incur sinful or negative reactions)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Acts performed strictly for body maintenance without possessiveness yield no karmic bondage.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Mastering impulse control and abandoning possessiveness prevents anxiety and emotional entanglement.
